steps.title: Outline the head
steps.instruction: Type the changed lines, then press Run. The turtle starts in the center, facing right.
steps.explain: Use four equal sides and quarter turns.
steps.question: Where will the turtle finish?
steps.answer: At the bottom-left corner, facing right.

steps.title: Fill the head

steps.question: Why does the fill finish after the loop?
steps.answer: All four sides must be traced first.

steps.title: Place the first eye
steps.instruction: Type the changed lines, then press Run. Keep the rest of your working code.
steps.explain: Move 50 units right and 130 up from the corner. Two dots at one spot make an eye.
steps.expected: One white eye with a dark pupil.
steps.question: Which dot belongs first?
steps.answer: The larger white dot, so the pupil stays visible on top.

steps.title: Move to the other eye
steps.instruction: Type the changed lines, then press Run. Keep the rest of your working code.
steps.explain: Move sideways from the first eye. Both eyes stay at the same height.
steps.question: Does this need a list of coordinates?
steps.answer: No. Move 100 units from the first eye to place the next one.

steps.title: Draw its mouth
steps.instruction: Type the changed lines, then press Run. Keep the rest of your working code.
steps.explain: Return left, move down, then draw across. Keep the pen lifted until you reach the mouth.
steps.expected: A straight mouth below the eyes.
steps.question: Which movement changes how low the mouth is?
steps.answer: The forward(70) after the downward turn.

steps.instruction: Change one size, position, or color. Predict the result, then run. Try a second change after checking the first.
steps.explain: Keep your working program while you experiment. If an edit has an unexpected effect, undo that one edit and run again.
steps.question: Show a partner one edit. Why did that line change the picture?
